title: Kazakhstan Again Sentences Activists for Supposed Attempt to Seize Power
author: Albert Otkjær
text:
Credit: Andrey Olesko on Unsplash
On September 8, five men were sentenced to between five and five-and-a-half years in prison after standing trial in an Almaty courtroom for supposedly attempting to seize control of power in Kazakhstan last year. The judges found all five suspects guilty not only of advocating for the violent seizure of power, but also of organizing mass unrest against authorities in the country and a seizure of the presidential residence, known as Akorda.Several of the convicted have a past in activism, having taken part in multiple civil protests in the country over the years. While doors were closed for the hearings, the case sparked some attention from both activists and national human rights organizations. Along with criticizing the verdict, focus was also given to similar cases that had targeted activists previously. These types of court cases, activists argue, are part of a strategy employed by the Kazakh government to control opposition in the country.[...]
